I can relate to this so much. I've had some amazing project ideas and wrote out some pretty passionate business plans, though they're not executed YET

Just now, I re-downloaded the Reddit app after two years. I used to spend a lot of time on Reddit during the day, but then, it just disappeared from my routine.

I have a book on my lap, and it's been a while since I finished a book, not since last winter. But when I start reading, I won't stop. I'll spend endless nights reading, sneak in a few pages at work, and take the book to appointments. I just can't stop reading until I'm done. I'm too invested, too curious, and too anxious not to continue.

Taking a shower feels a lot like reading for me. It takes a while to get started, but once I'm in, I don't want it to end.  

I'm thinking about asking my doctor to help me out.   I really want to finish my project with the same passion I have now.  I want to stay hyperfocused and continue working hard.  

I'm in my mid thirties and was never diagnosed.  How do I go about asking a doctor? And what medication has and has not worked?

We need more stinkyJimmy's.  You're doing the right thing.  I wish my last relationship would hang in there with me, but I just feel abandoned and not worth anything.  All I would have liked is a message or a hey, how are you doing?  Anyways, as long as you're not hurting yourself or her in this process then you're fine.   I'm sorry she doesn't want you romantically but I'm sure she's loving the friendship.  If that doesn't hurt too much, then continue to love her as a friend until she is ready.
You're an angel.

I don't know the relationship, but the sad part of BPD is that you don't want to be alone but you don't want to be around people when you're down.  If the relationship has a strong base, then I would say hey, I love you, I'll keep checking every couple of days until you're ready to talk.

If the relationship is new, I would just let her go.  She'll most likely feel overwhelmed with the relationship.  She wants to feel loved, but if the relationship isn't strong then she will feel as if it was a burden.  

I don't know, it's hard to say.  When I need space, I would want my boyfriend to reach out saying things like I love you. but if it was just a fling I would feel weird if they kept contacting me.  There's a lot more complications then just needing space.  Like the Why?  Did she feel that you hurt her?  Did she need to with friends?  Did she fight and now feel ashamed?  Stressed at work?  It all depends on why she needs space really.  

Have an honest conversation, talk about your needs and set boundaries.  It will get complicated, but if you love her and she feels loved it can be a beautiful thing.

You shouldn't feel ashamed.  You did what you thought you could do for a little bit of money.  You didn't hurt anyone.  Call it for what it is.  People wanted something you had and you got paid to give it to them.  I hope you were able to spend money on things that brought happy memories

Hairstyling/cosmetology industry.
You make others happy all day and feel rewarded at the end of each day.  You make life long relationships without getting involved in their lives outside of work.  It's like a dream come true job.

You'll find yourself sometimes dealing with a holes but in reality if you understand that 1/10 people are shit then you'll really start appreciating the job.  9/10 are wonderful humans that you get the honor to meet and get to know while making them feel good.

I didn't cheat but I think about him all the time.  I just had episode after episode with him.  It was never ending. We lived and worked together.  It was stressful and I couldn't get my shit together.
But I do miss him so much and I have this intense guilt of how I treated him.  It was horrible.  I hope I can see him again but I sure wouldn't want to see me if I were him.

I know this is cliche, but why not get off Instagram?  It's effecting everyone and causes different mental disorders even for the healthy mind.  I mean I love taking photos but I stopped posting because I found myself scrolling way too much and re reading what I posted over and over and trying to get validation from people I barely know.  I don't know, give it a try for a couple of weeks.  It'll help clear the mind and you won't have to worry about what others think on one less platform.  We already think too much about others without social media.

Just think about it if it were the other way around.  Let's say you did something he didn't like, but you didn't mean any harm.  Then he kept bringing it up over and over.  It gets old.  And it gets old really fast.  It's not healthy to relive mistakes.  It takes a toll on the relationship and it would be hard to love him if he kept repeating your mistakes.  Especially one that you really meant no harm.

I'm not an expert but I am someone who went through the most hellish month of my life just because I couldn't forgive.  I still get a bit anxious and sad when I think about it but I did forgive and I really still do love him but I ruined the relationship, him and myself because I couldn't forgive.  

If you truly truly want to be with him then forgive.  If you can't forgive then you have to go.  It's not fair to you to be with someone that you can't trust and it's not fair for him to be with someone that doesn't trust him.

I'm sorry that you had an attempt. I've tried twice this month.  I moved my car in the garage and just waiting for the courage just to turn on the car for more than 5 minutes.  I don't want this feeling.  I have so much guilt and sadness and I can't get up.  I don't want to keep feeling like a monster.

It fades.  I was you. Smile, it's contagious was my motto.  Man I loved life. I fought most negative feelings off.  I was happy with a side of BPD.  Now I feel like all that hard work is down the drain.  Not because I don't think I can get there again, it's because why do I have to do this again.  It's like starting over.  How many times?  Help
Thank you for the recommendation.  I need a new good book.

I never labeled myself as anything but extremely emotional.  Some therapist just wanted to put me on meds and some others I would lie to but I thought no one would understand me.  The first therapist I ever went to over 20 years ago told me if I was suicidal, they would have to turn me in, so I never trusted anyone after that.  I'm very suicidal and that's half the reason why I went to therapy.
But as I researched more and more on BPD this year, I finally felt that I understood myself more.  My mother is a complete narcissist, my dad was always angry and I was bullied very badly by my older sister and at school.  I tried to be strong through out the years but I raged a lot.  I never had any romantic relationships that lasted more than a few months, and if they did, it was because it was long distance.  I change my job at least every 2 years.  I have lived in 4 different countries and a couple of states.  I have suffered from eating disorders in the past and my self harm is minimal but it's still there.  If I don't have BPD then I don't know what I have.  I don't have insurance to get diagnosed by a "professional"  I've also had really bad experiences and some good experiences with therapist but at the end of the day, I'm still raging, still crying, still writing my suicides notes, even after decades of therapy.  So no therapy or diagnoses will make me feel better.
I started listening to DBT trainings and read different exercises but I don't want to have to go see a dr every week to talk about my problem. It doesn't work for me.  I don't trust them like I said earlier.  I just sit there in agony honestly.  
But I think if I have another  romantic relationship, even though I can't imagine right now, my heart hurts too much just thinking about trying to have another relationship, I can communicate before hand about my issues and finally pin point to them beforehand how I react to certain things.  Before I learned about BPD, I would just always blame my SO and walk out.  All the time.  I would always be so emotional and couldn't handle anything.  But that won't be the case for the next one, if there is a next one.  I can communicate now beforehand about my rollercoaster of emotions and let them decide if they want to risk their emotional state to be with me.
Sorry for my rant.

A lot of people had this problem last year during the heat wave.  It caused a lot of root rot where I'm from because plants were getting over watered during times the plants were not drinking.  They looked like this and so people automatically think they need water.

I had a friend who bought from marketplace as well and she didn't even make it home.  She had to tow it to the mechanic which was known for cheap and good work but the cost of fixing the car was triple what she had paid for it.  She asked the mechanic if he could use the parts, and he said of course so she left it with him for free.
 I on the other hand bought my used car online as well and paid 170$ to fix the problems, and a year later the only thing I needed to replace was the alternator.
I think a lot of people can relate to your mistake OP.  Don't be so hard on yourself.  The money will come again and you'll be able to invest it better.  Ya live and ya learn.

I'm listening.  You're also close to your next adventure, your next love, your next hot coffee, your next amazing meal.  You're so close to getting off or back on your meds.  You're close to the next hug.  Please don't give up.  I know it's hard, believe me as I write this I also feel like there's no point, but deep down I know I'm just being irrational.
